highInjuryNetwork.method: Fatal and serious-injury crashes per mile. Stored road lines are cut into pieces of about 0.5 mile. Each crash goes to the nearest piece within 50 meters. Pieces shorter than 0.25 mile are measured as 0.25 mile.

sourceCheck.note: Lincoln County, Nevada only. After the hosted journey, the case numbers it stored were read from the hosted database, read-only: 12 fatal crashes (6 in 2022, 4 in 2023, 2 in 2024; 12 people killed). They are the same 12 state case numbers that NHTSA's FARS national annual files for 2022, 2023 and 2024 hold for state 32, county 17, read with a script that uses no OpenPlan code. NHTSA's query service answered HTTP 403 to an automated request, so this compares OpenPlan with the published files it reads, not with a second NHTSA product. Sierra County (CCRS) and the tribal area were not checked this way.

limits.text: No PDF/UA check was run on the exported PDFs.
No keyboard-only or screen-reader pass was made.
No planner reviewed whether the PDFs are useful. Every check in this record was run by an agent.
FARS records fatal crashes only, so the Nevada county and tribal area counts omit serious injuries.
Crash counts were compared with the source's published files for Lincoln County only; the California county and the tribal area counts are the sources' own and were not confirmed independently.
The SS4A section text was written by an agent from public sources and says so in its first sentence. No county or tribe prepared, reviewed, adopted or submitted it, and it speaks for none of them.

The benefit-cost ratio rests on one treated segment, one assumed crash modification factor and an incomplete cost. It shows that the screen and the export work, not that any project is cost-effective.

The exported PDFs carry the product's own [VERIFY] markers on items it did not read from a primary source: the countermeasure list's factor notes, the attachment list and the action plan component names.

The two comments in each campaign were entered by the proof run and say so in their own text. They represent no one. Each safety action plan counts them as approved public comments toward its engagement component without that label.

The declared hand check for stored codes was not met. The severity-coverage code it was written for is gone, but the PDFs print other stored identifiers as they are kept (a benefit-cost status and ledger name, crash source ids, a segment id, template and schema names, repository file paths), and each plan's cover prints its creation time in UTC with no zone named.

The checker re-reads every text item in each PDF but does not render the map page again. That the high-injury map is drawn on the recorded page rests on the journey's own count of highlight-colored pixels on that page, whose image hash is recorded, and on the lead agent's separate render and look at all six map pages.
The hosted site prints PDFs in one font family, so headings that are serif on a workstation print in the same sans-serif face as the body.
